coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Grudge
You're Still Carrying
coverDek: For the apology that never came, the wound you keep reopening, and the freedom waiting on the other side of letting go.

points.hook: Lord, I've been waiting for an apology that may never come, and I'm tired of letting their silence set my release date.
paragraphs: Father, I keep holding the door open for a confession I may never get, as if my freedom is locked behind their willingness to admit what they did. Teach me that forgiveness was never a transaction I needed their signature on — it's a transfer I make with You, for my own sake, long before they ever say sorry, if they ever do at all.
points.verseText: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.

points.hook: I decree it today: the chain between me and what they did to me is broken, in Jesus' name!
paragraphs: I will not spend another year handcuffed to a moment they've probably forgotten! I cut the cord between my past and my peace right now — by the blood of Jesus, I release what was done to me, and I refuse to let one wound keep writing the rest of my story! Every root of bitterness trying to grow in my heart, I pull it up from the bottom, in the mighty name of Jesus!
points.verseText: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled.

points.hook: Notice where you're holding it — the clenched jaw, the tight chest, the breath you take before you say their name.
paragraphs: Your body has been keeping the account your mouth says is closed. I'm not asking you to pretend it didn't hurt or rush past what's still tender — I'm asking you to let Me into the places you've been guarding, the tightness that flares every time their name comes up. Unforgiveness isn't just a decision you haven't made yet; it's a weight your shoulders have been carrying for you. Let Me carry it instead, so your body can finally believe what your mouth has been saying.
points.verseText: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

points.hook: We don't do this alone — bring your hurt into the light and let the family carry it with you.
paragraphs: Church, somebody reading this is still nursing a wound from somebody who sat near them — and we need to say it plainly: unforgiveness in the body doesn't just hurt you, it chips at all of us. So we're praying together today, for the sister still stung by what was said about her, for the brother still smarting from who left when it mattered. Lord, heal what's festering between us before it festers any further, and teach us to forgive as fast as we were forgiven — grace was never meant to stop moving once it reached us.
points.verseText: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.

points.hook: Baby, the person you haven't forgiven yet might be the one standing closest to you — you.
paragraphs: I know you've replayed it a hundred times — the mistake, the way you handled it, the years you can't get back. Sweetheart, you've already apologized to yourself more than most people ever say out loud, and it's time to accept the pardon. God isn't holding it over you, so stop holding it over you. Lay it down tonight. You don't have to earn forgiveness you were already given — you just have to receive it.
points.verseText: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

cta.closingLine: If this spoke to you, let's stay connected.
